Jacob Duffy to Shubman Gill, out Bowled!! And he's gone through the gate. What an anticlimax! Jacob Duffy wears a smile on his face and looks at the skies in relief. Has been a tough game for him, being taken for 180 runs. But Gill walks back gutted. He's furious inside as he heads back. Pant feels his pain as well. The Indian team gives him a pat on the back for his knock. But out of nowhere, Duffy got this ball to nip back in a fair bit and trouble Gill on the front foot push. The ball hit the pad and and ricocheted onto the off stump. Another wicket against the run of play. Being on 98 and trying to get to the hundred before stumps might have played its part in this dismissal, Gill pushed with the bat in front instead of defending with it being close to the pad, leaving a gap for the ball to sneak through. Devdutt Padikkal (1/3): [How did that innings feel?] Yeah, it was good. It's always great to get some runs. I think it was important that me and KL started off the day well. It was important that we didn't let them back into the game. And I think we did that pretty well today. [Tell us about that partnership and what you were saying to each other and what it was like to be at the other end] Yeah, like I said, it was important that we got through that first session. I think if they were able to pick up a couple of wickets early, it would have put us in a bit of a difficult position. But I think that was the conversation, just building that partnership and taking it as deep as possible. And once we were able to do that, then it was our turn to put pressure back on them. And I think we did that well.

Padikkal (2/3): [What did you enjoy about the conditions here at the Basin Reserve?] Yeah, it's a great ground. It's my first time in New Zealand. I really enjoyed being out here and this was a great venue to play cricket at. And hopefully we can continue to play some good cricket and get a win with us. [Some of your teammates have played in New Zealand before. What did they tell you about conditions here and how did you change your game to suit them?] Yeah, definitely. I think we expected a lot, a lot of grass on the wicket. We expected a lot of movement. It's probably not panned out that way. It's been much flatter than we expected. But at the same time, it's important that you respect the conditions that are in front of you. I think it was important that we continue to score big. And that's the conversation in the dressing room as well. Everyone's really confident. Everyone's had a lot of preparation behind them coming into this Test match and that shows.

Padikkal (3/3): [You talk about batting long periods. Have you talked about a number, a target that you'd like to get or is it just about batting time?] Not yet. We are not looking too far ahead. It's important that we take one session at a time. I think definitely we are in a really good position right now. But it's important that we really extend that lead as much as possible so that we can put more pressure on them.

New Zealand players leave the field. Meanwhile Pant and AK47 first tap their bats then punch gloves/hands, then repeat the same thing again just before they crossed the boundary. Some of kind of superstition there for sure. Oh these batters! Jadeja and Conway have some banter. Jadeja pretends to throw something at Conway and then they both hug each other. Conway has his left arm over Jadeja's neck, pulls him closer as they chat with big smiles on their faces and disappear into the background. Pure CSK love there!

So this is India's game to move now. Lead is 118, they have 6 wickets in hand and they will be looking to add another 120 odd tomorrow morning. And more importantly hope that the pitch starts to misbehave drastically. Because if it stays the same, bowling is going to be tough for the Indians as well. First swell the lead past 250 and take it from there could be approach. New Zealand need to make dramatic progress to pull off a win here, looks very unlikely though but you never know. The hosts managed to beat England by 1 run here back in 2023 in the closing moments of the Test match. See you all tomorrow morning again for Day 4 action.
